summaryText:
In this Sunday message at Impact Church, guest speaker John Bevere shared from his newest book on the second coming of Jesus. He explained that he avoided the subject for decades, fearing it would produce lazy or argumentative believers. After the Holy Spirit led him to study it beginning in 2021, he found the opposite in his own life: deeper passion for Jesus, greater tenderness toward his family, and a fresh hunger to see people come to Christ. He noted how often Scripture speaks about Christ's return and asked what wisdom God has in that emphasis.

Bevere compared those who missed Jesus at His first coming with Simeon and Anna, who recognized the infant Messiah. Luke 2:25 describes Simeon as righteous, devout, and eagerly waiting. Bevere pointed out that the New Testament calls believers to this same eager expectation. He taught that what we set our sights on shapes what we think about, especially when our minds are at rest, and he invited the congregation to ask where their thoughts naturally go.

A central teaching was 1 John 3:3, that everyone who has this hope purifies themselves. Bevere distinguished between justification, what Christ's blood does for us once, and sanctification, the ongoing work in which we cooperate with God. He suggested that when eager expectation fades, believers can drift toward unforgiveness, harshness toward others, and a loss of self-control. He also addressed those who struggle with besetting temptations, encouraging them that a heart fixed on Jesus brings real power to change.

Using 2 Peter 3 and the idea that a day with the Lord is like a thousand years, Bevere argued that God is not deceiving us when He says He is coming soon. He suggested God is protecting every generation by keeping us watchful. The parable of the ten virgins showed that endurance matters, and he urged listeners not to be fooled by any message that treats grace as permission to ignore holiness. Grace empowers obedience, and obedience keeps us in close fellowship with Jesus, so that we can be confident rather than ashamed when He returns.

He closed with the image of a bride making herself ready, and invited everyone to give themselves fully to Jesus, who laid down His life for His bride. Many stood and prayed aloud together to surrender their lives to Christ.
mainPoints: Scripture calls believers to live in eager, ongoing expectation of Jesus' return, setting our minds on heaven rather than earthly things, as Simeon and Anna did.
That eager expectation gives us power to purify ourselves and walk in obedience, and God's grace empowers holy living rather than excusing sin, so we can endure to the end like the wise virgins.
We are called to stay dressed for action and make ourselves ready as Christ's bride, so we can meet Him with confidence instead of shame by giving ourselves fully to Him.

versesMentioned.text: At midnight the cry rang out: 'Here's the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!'
You desire but do not have, so you kill. You covet but you cannot get what you want, so you quarrel and fight. You do not have because you do not ask God.
Therefore I want the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands without anger or disputing.
your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
Now there was a man in Jerusalem called Simeon, who was righteous and devout. He was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.

Be dressed ready for service and keep your lamps burning, like servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks they can immediately open the door for him.
therefore you do not lack any spiritual gift as you eagerly wait for our Lord Jesus Christ to be revealed.
Now there is in store for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that day, and not only to me, but also to all who have longed for his appearing.
so Christ was sacrificed once to take away the sins of many; and he will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who are waiting for him.
Since, then, you have been raised with Christ, set your hearts on things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.

For, as I have often told you before and now tell you again even with tears, many live as enemies of the cross of Christ. Their destiny is destruction, their god is their stomach, and their glory is in their shame. Their mind is set on earthly things. But our citizenship is in heaven. And we eagerly await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ,

Dear friends, now we are children of God, and what we will be has not yet been made known. But we know that when Christ appears, we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is. All who have this hope in him purify themselves, just as he is pure.
Since we have these promises, dear friends, let us purify ourselves from everything that contaminates body and spirit, perfecting holiness out of reverence for God.
Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places. All these are the beginning of birth pains.
Then will appear the sign of the Son of Man in heaven. And then all the peoples of the earth will mourn when they see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven, with power and great glory.
But suppose that servant is wicked and says to himself, 'My master is staying away a long time,' and he then begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards.
bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
Jesus said, 'Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.' And they divided up his clothes by casting lots.

Above all, you must understand that in the last days scoffers will come, scoffing and following their own evil desires. They will say, "Where is this 'coming' he promised? Ever since our ancestors died, everything goes on as it has since the beginning of creation."
But do not forget this one thing, dear friends: With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.
but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for when you eat from it you will certainly die.
By the sweat of your brow you will eat your food until you return to the ground, since from it you were taken; for dust you are and to dust you will return.
You too, be patient and stand firm, because the Lord's coming is near.
The end of all things is near. Therefore be alert and of sober mind so that you may pray.
I am coming soon. Hold on to what you have, so that no one will take your crown.
Look, I am coming soon! My reward is with me, and I will give to each person according to what they have done.
Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things have happened.
At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom. Five of them were foolish and five were wise.
You are the light of the world. A town built on a hill cannot be hidden.
The foolish ones said to the wise, 'Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.'
but the one who stands firm to the end will be saved.

For of this you can be sure: No immoral, impure or greedy person, such a person is an idolater, has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God. Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of such things God's wrath comes on those who are disobedient.
Be very careful, then, how you live, not as unwise but as wise,

For certain individuals whose condemnation was written about long ago have secretly slipped in among you. They are ungodly people, who pervert the grace of our God into a license for immorality and deny Jesus Christ our only Sovereign and Lord.
What is more, I consider everything a loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I have lost all things. I consider them garbage, that I may gain Christ
Whoever claims to live in him must live as Jesus did.
The one who keeps God's commands lives in him, and he in them. And this is how we know that he lives in us: We know it by the Spirit he gave us.
Whoever has my commands and keeps them is the one who loves me. The one who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I too will love them and show myself to them.

Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.
You adulterous people, don't you know that friendship with the world means enmity against God? Therefore, anyone who chooses to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God.
And now, dear children, continue in him, so that when he appears we may be confident and unashamed before him at his coming.

Let us rejoice and be glad and give him glory! For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready. Fine linen, bright and clean, was given her to wear. (Fine linen stands for the righteous acts of God's holy people.)
Look, I come like a thief! Blessed is the one who stays awake and remains clothed, so as not to go naked and be shamefully exposed.
fixing our eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of faith. For the joy set before him he endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Then he said to them all: 'Whoever wants to be a disciple of mine must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.'
For it is with your heart that you believe and are justified, and it is with your mouth that you profess your faith and are saved.

Monday.scripture: Luke 12:35 (NIV): Be dressed ready for service and keep your lamps burning.
Monday.focus: Living in eager expectation of Jesus' return rather than a casual interest.
Monday.action: Read Matthew 25:1-13 slowly. Write down one specific way you can live ready for Jesus this week.
Monday.prayer: Lord Jesus, stir in me a real longing for Your return. Keep my lamp burning and my heart ready each day. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Colossians 3:2 (NIV): Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
Tuesday.focus: Setting your sights on heaven and noticing where your mind goes when it is at rest.
Tuesday.action: Pay attention today to where your thoughts drift in quiet moments. Replace one stretch of scrolling or idle screen time with 10 minutes of prayer or Scripture.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, show me where my mind wanders. Teach me to fix my thoughts on You and on the things that last. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: 1 John 3:3 (NIV): All who have this hope in him purify themselves, just as he is pure.
Wednesday.focus: Hope in Christ's return gives us power to cooperate with God in growing in holiness.
Wednesday.action: Ask God to show you one area where you need to grow. Take one practical step, such as removing a distraction or talking with a trusted believer or pastor for support.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, thank You that Your blood has made me clean. Help me cooperate with You as You make me more like You. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Luke 6:28 (NIV): Bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
Thursday.focus: Letting go of offense and choosing forgiveness as we wait for the Lord.
Thursday.action: Pray by name for someone who has hurt or frustrated you. If it is safe and healthy, send an encouraging message or do one kind thing for them.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, You forgave me before I ever asked. Give me a soft heart to forgive and to love others as You love me. Amen.

Friday.scripture: 1 John 2:28 (NIV): Continue in him, so that when he appears we may be confident and unashamed before him at his coming.
Friday.focus: Staying close to Jesus through obedience so that we can be confident, not ashamed.
Friday.action: Choose one command of Jesus you have been putting off, such as serving, forgiving, or sharing your faith. Obey it today.
Friday.prayer: Jesus, I want to remain close to You. Give me courage to obey You today so that I can meet You with confidence. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Revelation 19:7 (NIV): The wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready.
Saturday.focus: Making ourselves ready and giving our whole lives to Jesus.
Saturday.action: Write a short prayer of surrender to Jesus. Then share this week's sermon with a friend or family member who may be encouraged by it.
Saturday.prayer: Lord Jesus, I give You my spirit, soul, and body. Make me ready for Your return, and use me to point others to You. Amen.

title: Is Jesus Coming Back Soon? How to Be Ready - John Bevere
